name: keras_tfdata
title: Keras functional classifier fed by a tf.data pipeline
origin: re-created from the Sprint-2 audit's Keras / tf.data probe (ROADMAP b.1)

expected.defect: the scaler is fitted on the whole matrix two lines before train_test_split
expected.why: the validation half's statistics are already inside the training features

expected.defect: the tf.data normalise closure captures a mean and std computed over every row, then maps it over both splits
expected.why: a second, quieter leak on the tf.data path - the constants baked into the graph saw the validation rows
the AUC reported changes run to run for reasons that have nothing to do with the model

expected.defect: a sigmoid output layer paired with BinaryCrossentropy(from_logits=True)
expected.why: the loss applies its own sigmoid to an already-squashed value, so the gradients vanish and the model trains to nothing
expected.relabelled: ANA-7, 2026-09-09: this was labelled MLV402, which is the torch rule (nn.BCELoss / F.binary_cross_entropy) and can never resolve on a Keras program. The Keras from_logits contradiction is MLV709; the defect, the line and the severity are unchanged.

expected.defect: nothing seeds tensorflow, numpy or the split
expected.why: shuffle(4096), the split and the layer initialisers are all unseeded

forbidden.why: the tf.data chain is shuffle -> batch -> prefetch with no take()/skip() holdout in it, so nothing is re-drawn across a split boundary
build_model() calls model.compile(...) at line 19 before anything is fitted
Keras model.fit owns the loop - there is no hand-written gradient update in this project
same - no backward()/step() pair exists here
model.eval() is a torch idiom; a Keras model has no such call and model.evaluate is not an inference-mode bug
torch.no_grad() has no meaning in a TensorFlow program
the functional API composes layers by call, not by registering submodules on an nn.Module
